source.version: PsyArXiv preprint v1 (doi 10.31234/osf.io/rz5s4_v1; OSF file 'Homogenization pre-print v1.1.pdf', page header 'Pre-print, 15 April, 2026', posted 2026-04-21), 11 pages, read in memory from osf.io/download/wxdbt. The journal version of record (Behaviour & Information Technology, online 2026-08-31, doi 10.1080/0144929x.2026.2726451) and the ECCE 2026 short paper (doi 10.1145/3822301.3822304) were not reachable; Crossref gives no abstract for either, so this form does not confirm that their numbers match the preprint. Fix verification on 2026-10-09 read the complete preprint PDF, including references through p. 11, plus public OSF preprint metadata (https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/rz5s4_v1/), project file listings, and the data/code downloads in memory to confirm availability. All reported statistics remain sourced to the preprint PDF; no analysis was rerun.
source.title_on_document: Does Generative AI Make Us Think Alike? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Homogenization Effects in Human–AI Co-Creation

supplement.where: https://osf.io/ujpag/ (linked by the public OSF preprint metadata, not in the PDF)
supplement.holds: The public OSF preprint metadata links the project containing Meta-analysis/Data/dataset.xlsx (https://osf.io/download/bvzw3/) and Meta-analysis/Analysis/analysis.R (https://osf.io/download/x69ay/). File listings and both downloads were verified in memory on 2026-10-09. The PDF itself mentions no supplement or data/code repository and has no appended supplement; Table 1 (p. 5) lists comparisons and Figure 2 (p. 7) plots effect sizes without tabulating the study-level estimates.

paper_design_summary: Systematic review and three-level meta-analysis (R, metafor) of experimental and quasi-experimental studies that compare people creating with generative AI against people creating without it on collective-level homogenization of creative output. The search covered 2022 to February 25, 2026 and yielded 18 articles, 19 studies, and 61 Cohen's d effect sizes, coded so that positive values mean more homogenization with AI. Moderator analyses test task type, during versus after AI use, and controlled versus real-world quasi-experiments.

studies.label: Three-level meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation (19 studies, 61 effect sizes)

participants.who: Corpus of 18 eligible articles contributing 19 (quasi-)experimental studies and 61 effect sizes with sampling variances: 16 controlled experiments and 3 real-world quasi-experiments (pre- vs post-ChatGPT essays and articles; artworks before vs after AI adoption). Participant totals are not reported.
participants.quote: In total, the 18 eligible articles contributed 19 eligible (quasi-)experimental studies, and 61 effect sizes with accompanying sampling variances to be meta-analyzed.
participants.locator: p. 4, Section 3.4; p. 4, Figure 1; p. 5, Table 1

ai_tool.name_model: Various, as listed in Table 1: GPT-3, InstructGPT, GPT-3.5/ChatGPT-3.5, GPT-4, ChatGPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, ChatGPT o1-preview, Midjourney 4
ai_tool.how_used: Mixed across included studies: open access to a chatbot, AI-generated example ideas or idea lists, text suggestions, feedback, co-writing, persona-based plots, and image idea examples (p. 5, Table 1).

task.description: Mixed creative tasks coded into four categories: divergent thinking (e.g., alternative uses test), idea generation, writing (essays, short stories), and visual art and design (p. 5, Section 3.5).

outcomes.name: Pooled homogenization of creative output across people (sign reversed: positive d = less collective diversity with AI); unit of the meta-analysis is the effect size
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: The measure code embedding_similarity identifies one included measure family; these synthesis results also include aggregates of expert ratings, including visual-design study [64], and cannot be interpreted as a single embedding-similarity measure (p. 3, Section 3.2; p. 5, Table 1). Cohen's d was extracted or computed from source-study statistics, with positive values coded as greater homogenization. A common participant-level standard deviation is not specified. These are synthesis estimates, not new participant-level observations (pp. 3-4, Section 3.4). The reported exclusion of one influential study is a sensitivity analysis of the same pooled outcome (p. 6, Section 4.1.2).

contrasts.control_arm: Humans not using AI co-creatively (some studies use active comparators: oblique strategies, human example ideas, a human dyad; quasi-experiments compare pre- vs post-ChatGPT output)
contrasts.reported: Pooled d = .334, 95% CI [.094, .574] (19 studies, 61 effect sizes); Q(df = 60) = 2850.50, p < .001; about 68% between-study and 31% within-study variance. Sensitivity without one influential study (3 effect sizes): d = .247, 95% CI [.065, .429]; Q(df = 57) = 2524.19, p < .001. Egger-type test among peer-reviewed studies (14 studies, 53 effect sizes): b = 5.36, p = .144. Positive d = greater homogenization in AI co-created output.

diversity_detail.metric: Mixed collective semantic homogenization measures: pairwise cosine distances between transformer-based sentence embeddings of participant responses, and aggregates of expert ratings of meanings relative to the sample (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: No common embedding model is specified in the preprint (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Participant responses compared with all responses in a study sample, or expert ratings of meanings relative to those produced in that sample. The preprint does not enumerate each study's exact pair, condition, or reference-set implementation (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Study effect sizes and sampling variances enter a three-level meta-analysis modeling sampling, within-study, and between-study variance; reported confidence intervals are for the pooled effect. The preprint does not establish a common participant-level basis for every input sampling variance (pp. 3-5, Sections 3.4-3.5; pp. 5-6, Sections 4.1.1-4.1.2).
diversity_detail.notes: Cohen's d was extracted or computed from source-study statistics, with positive values coded as greater homogenization. A common participant-level standard deviation is not specified. These are synthesis estimates, not new participant-level observations (pp. 3-4, Section 3.4).

outcomes.name: Homogenization by task type (moderator analysis; sign reversed: positive d = less collective diversity with AI)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: The measure code embedding_similarity identifies one included measure family; these synthesis results also include aggregates of expert ratings, including visual-design study [64], and cannot be interpreted as a single embedding-similarity measure (p. 3, Section 3.2; p. 5, Table 1). Cohen's d was extracted or computed from source-study statistics, with positive values coded as greater homogenization. A common participant-level standard deviation is not specified. These are synthesis estimates, not new participant-level observations (pp. 3-4, Section 3.4).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Humans co-creating with generative AI, by task type (idea generation shown as the headline)
contrasts.reported: Qm(df = 3) = 17.12, p = .002. Idea generation d = 0.70, 95% CI [.30, 1.10] (5 studies, 14 effect sizes); divergent thinking d = 0.12, 95% CI [-.285, .518] (4 studies, 27); writing d = 0.27, 95% CI [-.078, .613] (9 studies, 18); visual art and design d = 0.27, 95% CI [-.555, 1.088] (2 studies, 2). Qe(df = 57) = 1860.92, p < .001. Holm-corrected divergent thinking - idea generation Mdiff = -0.582, se 0.193, p = .015.
contrasts.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2; p. 7, Table 2 and Figure 2b

diversity_detail.metric: Mixed collective semantic homogenization measures: pairwise cosine distances between transformer-based sentence embeddings of participant responses, and aggregates of expert ratings of meanings relative to the sample (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: No common embedding model is specified in the preprint (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Participant responses compared with all responses in a study sample, or expert ratings of meanings relative to those produced in that sample. The preprint does not enumerate each study's exact pair, condition, or reference-set implementation (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Three-level moderator model without an intercept, using source-study effect sizes and sampling variances and modeling sampling, within-study, and between-study variance; task-specific confidence intervals and Holm-corrected pairwise comparisons of model-implied marginal means. A common participant-level basis for input sampling variances is not established (pp. 4-5, Sections 3.4-3.5; p. 6, Section 4.2; p. 7, Table 2).
diversity_detail.notes: Cohen's d was extracted or computed from source-study statistics, with positive values coded as greater homogenization. A common participant-level standard deviation is not specified. These are synthesis estimates, not new participant-level observations (pp. 3-4, Section 3.4).

outcomes.name: Homogenization during co-creation, divergent thinking and idea generation subset (sign reversed)
outcomes.question: across_people

contrasts.treatment_arm: Humans co-creating with generative AI, outcome measured during co-creation
contrasts.reported: Intercept (during co-creation) d = .453, 95% CI [.048, .953] (8 studies, 35 effect sizes), as printed; during-vs-after contrast b = -.331, 95% CI [-.771, .110]; Qm(1) = 2.17, p = .141; Qe(df = 39) = 1111.59, p < .001.

outcomes.name: Homogenization after AI use (unassisted later tasks; sign reversed)
outcomes.question: after_ai

contrasts.treatment_arm: Humans who previously co-created with generative AI, outcome measured after AI use
contrasts.control_arm: Humans who did not use AI
contrasts.reported: After AI use alone: d = .414, 95% CI [.235, .593] (2 studies [37, 70], 6 effect sizes); Q(df = 5) = 5.75, p = .331; about 70% sampling and 30% within-study variance.

outcomes.name: Homogenization in real-world quasi-experiments, writing and visual tasks (sign reversed)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: The controlled-versus-quasi comparison combines writing and visual tasks and spans heterogeneous homogenization measures, including sentence-embedding comparisons and expert-rating aggregates. Expert-rating study [64] belongs to the controlled visual-design group, not the quasi-only pooled estimate. The quasi-only subset contains studies [46], [69], and [70] (1); the preprint does not specify a common metric, embedding model, or participant-level standard deviation for that subset. The measure code embedding_similarity identifies one included measure family, not a common measure for all reported results (p. 3, Section 3.2; p. 5, Table 1; pp. 6-7, Section 4.4).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Real-world output after ChatGPT release or AI adoption
contrasts.control_arm: Real-world output before ChatGPT release or AI adoption
contrasts.reported: Quasi-experiments alone: d = .303, 95% CI [.082, .524] (3 studies, 7 effect sizes); Q(df = 6) = 938.71, p < .001. Controlled experiments (same task types): d = .255, 95% CI [.034, .477] (8 studies, 13 effect sizes); quasi-vs-controlled contrast b = .042, 95% CI [-.358, .442]; Qm(df = 1) = .05, p = .837; Qe(df = 18) = 1017.61, p < .001.

diversity_detail.metric: Mixed semantic homogenization metrics in the writing/visual moderator analysis, including sentence-embedding comparisons and expert-rating aggregates in the controlled group. Metrics for the quasi-only subset are not separately enumerated (p. 3, Section 3.2; p. 5, Table 1; pp. 6-7, Section 4.4).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: No common embedding model is specified in the preprint (p. 3, Section 3.2).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Collective comparisons of writing or visual output. Quasi-experiments compare essays/articles before and after ChatGPT, or artworks before and after AI adoption; their exact within-corpus comparison sets are not specified in the preprint (p. 5, Table 1; pp. 6-7, Section 4.4).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Three-level model comparing controlled and quasi-experimental studies in matching task types, followed by a separate three-level meta-analysis of the quasi-only subset. Models use source-study effect sizes and sampling variances and distinguish sampling, within-study, and between-study variance. A common participant-level basis for the input variances is not established (pp. 4-5, Sections 3.4-3.5; pp. 6-7, Section 4.4).
diversity_detail.notes: Cohen's d was extracted or computed from source-study statistics, with positive values coded as greater homogenization. A common participant-level standard deviation is not specified. These are synthesis estimates, not new participant-level observations (pp. 3-4, Section 3.4).

synthesis.inclusion: Experimental studies (peer-reviewed or not, in English) comparing participants using generative AI (LLMs, image, music, or audio generators) in human-AI co-creation with participants not using it, with an outcome of collective-level homogenization (reduced diversity of meanings) of creative output, measured during or after AI use, and enough statistics to compute Cohen's d and its sampling variance. Surface-level lexical or stylistic similarity metrics and individual-level diversity measures were excluded. Searched Web of Science, ACM DL, PsycINFO, Google Scholar (first 200), arXiv, PsyArXiv, SSRN, ProQuest Dissertations from 2022; 18 articles, 19 studies (pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1-3.4).

pooled.comparison: All studies: AI co-creation vs no AI co-creation, homogenization
pooled.what_it_standardizes: Cohen's d extracted or computed from each study's reported statistics (one from raw data, two from digitized graphs); standardizer not further specified; positive = more homogenization with AI

pooled.comparison: Sensitivity: excluding one influential study (3 effect sizes)
Task type: idea generation (5 studies, 14 effect sizes)
Task type: divergent thinking (4 studies, 27 effect sizes)
Task type: writing (9 studies, 18 effect sizes)
Task type: visual art and design (2 studies, 2 effect sizes)

pooled.what_it_standardizes: Difference in model-implied marginal means of Cohen's d

pooled.comparison: During co-creation, divergent thinking and idea generation subset (8 studies, 35 effect sizes)
After minus during AI use (moderator contrast)
After AI use only (2 studies, 6 effect sizes)
Controlled experiments, writing and visual tasks (8 studies, 13 effect sizes)
Real-world quasi-experiments only (3 studies, 7 effect sizes)

eligibility.reason: Systematic review and three-level meta-analysis; it assigns no people to conditions and contributes no primary estimates. Its pooled numbers are quoted beside the atlas's, and its Table 1 (p. 5) is a source of candidate studies.

one_line_finding: Across 19 studies and 61 effect sizes, creating with generative AI made outputs more alike across people (pooled d = .334, 95% CI [.094, .574]), most clearly in idea generation tasks (d = 0.70, 95% CI [.30, 1.10]), and after AI use (d = .414, 95% CI [.235, .593]) (PsyArXiv preprint, p. 6, Sections 4.1 to 4.3).
